operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-101. The obligations of the Agreement on Government Procurement (Agreement on Government Procurement, General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 12 April 1979, Geneva (GATT 1979) ) apply to any procurement of eligible products by the Executive agencies listed in the Annex to this Order (eligible products are defined in Section 308 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979; 19 U.S.C. 2518(4) ). Such procurement shall be in accord with the policies and procedures of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (41 U.S.C. 401 et seq.).

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-101

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-102. The United States Trade Representative, hereinafter referred to as the Trade Representative, shall be responsible for interpretation of the Agreement. The Trade Representative shall seek the advice of the interagency organization established under Section 242(a) of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 (19 U.S.G. 1872(a)) and consult with affected Executive agencies, including the Office of Federal Procurement Policy.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-102

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-103. The interpretation of Article VIII: 1 of the Agreement shall be subject to the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-103

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-104. The Trade Representative shall determine, from time to time, the dollar equivalent of 150,000 Special Drawing Right units and shall publish that determination in the FEDERAL REGISTER. Procurement of less than 150,000 Special Drawing Right units is not subject to the Agreement or this Order (Article I: 1 (b) of the Agreement).

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-104

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-105. In order to ensure coordination of international trade policy with regard to the implementation of the Agreement, agencies shall consult in advance with the Trade Representative about negotiations with foreign governments or instrumentalities which concern government procurement.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-105

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-201. The functions vested in the President by Sections 301, 302, 304, 305 (c) and 306 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2511, 2512, 2514, 2515(c) and 2516) are delegated to the Trade Representative.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-201

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-202. Notwithstanding the delegation in Section 1-201, the Secretary of Defense is authorized, in accord with Section 302(b) (3) of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2512(b)(3)), to waive the prohibitions specified therein.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1-202
